claim: Papers whose reference lists are mostly conventional but include a small tail of atypical journal pairs are cited as hits about twice as often as baseline (9.11 vs 5 per 100; both-low 2.05).
agent_test: Open-mode selection test: pick the candidate that is a known frame plus one distant element versus all-near or all-far candidates; judge by blind rubric at equal tokens.

claim: Most science is conventional: under 4% of 1980s-1990s WoS papers have negative median z, yet about 41% have a negative 10th-percentile z.
agent_test: None; descriptive.

claim: Atypical-combination hit rate is higher in larger teams (tail novelty 36.1% solo to 49.7% for 3+); team size is a proxy for diverse knowledge.
agent_test: Compare one agent against a multi-sampled pool that recombines different frames at equal tokens.

claim: Uzzi-style journal-pair z-scores are weakly related to expert-judged novelty: one SD up in score U gives +7.47% 'new finding' tags with pseudo R2 0.33%.
agent_test: Do not use journal-pair z as a stand-in for novelty in agent scoring; validate any proxy against blind human labels first.

claim: The Wang-Veugelers-Stephan new-pair score W does not reproduce expert novelty tags; Bornmann advises using Lee et al.'s U and questioning W.
agent_test: Check any novelty proxy for convergent validity before using it to select.

claim: Atypicality barely predicts disruption at paper level (r=-0.05) and weakly predicts Sleeping Beauty status (r=0.08), yet the extreme groups differ (61% vs 36% in a disruptive class).
agent_test: Look for a threshold effect: does only an extreme-distance candidate beat the conventional one, and does a middle-distance candidate add nothing?

claim: Highly atypical papers are rare (2.3%) and their share fell from 3.9% (1970) to 1.4% (2000); journal embeddings reproduce z-scores at r=0.74.
agent_test: None.

claim: Content-based surprisal from a small language model (GPT-2 on Wikipedia) separates expert-labelled novel papers from others (Welch t=2.6, p=0.005, 25 of 80 novel) but flags maths-heavy and odd-style text as false alarms.
agent_test: Token-level surprisal of candidate text under the same model as a cheap novelty signal; test against blind rater novelty and against a style-matched control.

claim: Patent-class atypicality has a small positive effect on 5-year top-5% citation hits (8.88M patents).
agent_test: None for now; replicate the Uzzi pattern on a task bank instead.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas are rated more novel than expert human ideas when judged as ideas: 5.64 AI and 5.81 AI+rerank vs 4.84 human (79 reviewers, 49 ideas per condition).
agent_test: Same-task blind comparison of agent ideas vs baseline ideas, rated before any execution.

claim: That novelty advantage vanishes after execution: AI ideas lose 1.049 novelty points vs -0.010 for human ideas (N=43, FDR p=0.025); execution-stage means alone do not differ significantly.
agent_test: Rate candidate novelty before and after a verification step; report the drop. Equal token budget.

claim: Reviewer judgments of novelty are noisy: inter-reviewer pairwise agreement 56.1% vs 66.0% (NeurIPS 2021) and 71.9% (ICLR 2024).
agent_test: Use at least 3 raters and report agreement; do not trust a single rating.

claim: Frontier LLMs are poor novelty judges: best macro-F1 17.2 on RINoBench (1,381 ideas) and 0.0 F1 on the 'not novel' class for every model.
agent_test: Have the agent rate novelty of its own and baseline ideas against blind human labels; expect a positive-novelty bias.

claim: LLM judges disagree with human experts on non-obviousness (human-LLM agreement as low as 22%); LLM judges favour LLM-generated research questions (gpt-5.5 wins 82% / 52% vs experts giving the reference 78% / 56%). Mechanism evidence: GPT-4 picks its own text 73.5% of the time against two LLMs and humans and self-preference rises linearly with that skill; judges also favour lower-perplexity text.
agent_test: Judge candidates with a different model than the generator; compare win rates to human gold.

claim: LLM rankers do about as poorly as noisy humans at ranking ideas: Claude-3.5 pairwise 53.3% vs human consistency 56.1% in the Si study, though 71.4% was reported on a different quality task.
agent_test: Treat pairwise LLM ranking accuracy as task-specific; measure it on our own labels.

claim: Retrieval-grounded novelty checking helps a lot over zero-shot judging: 'not novel' accuracy 89.66% for the full pipeline vs 5-14% for ablations; TextGrad prompt 0.78 acc vs zero-shot 0.68.
agent_test: Add a prior-work retrieval check before accepting a novel candidate; measure the false 'novel' rate at equal tokens. (b22 and c15/c16 are the same paper, so one source.)

claim: RAG-style novelty detection beats direct LLM judging: RAG-KD 0.7453 / 0.7474 accuracy vs MOOSE 0.64 / 0.59; best K is 5-10.
agent_test: Vary the number of retrieved items K (5, 10, 20) in the novelty check.

claim: Hierarchical multi-step LLM scoring beats one-step zero-shot (RMSE down 17.3% to 35.4%) against reviewer novelty scores.
agent_test: Compare one-shot novelty rating vs decomposed per-facet rating.

claim: AI idea generators produce few distinct ideas: only 200 of 4,000 seed ideas were non-duplicate; model outputs are homogeneous (within-prompt similarity 0.821; cross-model 71-82%).
agent_test: Measure distinct-k of the agent's candidate set; test whether forced diverging frames raise it at equal tokens.

claim: Iterative novelty-boosting improves novelty rating in about half of cases (SciMON +54.4% to +57.8% of ideas), but gains come with generic added terms and the ground-truth paper idea is judged more novel in 85% of pairs.
agent_test: Test an explicit 'make more novel' revision pass against single-shot; check that gains are not term padding.

claim: Selecting concept pairs by predicted citation impact does not raise expert-rated interest (2.350 vs random 2.446 vs titles-only 2.414, 4,400+ ideas); LLM zero-shot interest AUC 67.44%.
agent_test: Do not select candidates by a citation-style prior; compare to random-pair and plain baselines.

claim: Novelty-check tools help a bit but not reliably in user studies: Scideator users used the checker about 6 times with no significant change in confidence (n=17).
agent_test: Weak; low priority.

claim: Generative AI raises individual creative output novelty (+6.7%; +8.1% with 5 ideas; low-creativity writers +10.7%) but makes stories more similar to each other.
agent_test: Show the agent 1 vs 5 prior candidate ideas and measure novelty and between-run similarity.

claim: A substantial share of LLM-agent 'novel' research output is not novel: 24.0% of 50 documents were plagiarism of one-to-one methodology; the AI-Scientist novelty checker marked all 10 ideas novel in one case study.
agent_test: Run novelty claims past retrieval before accepting; count how many pass.

claim: After ChatGPT, novelty scores in IS journals dropped about 0.176 SD (about 7 percentile points) for one group of papers; this is a post-2022 shift, not proven LLM causation.
agent_test: None.

claim: Co-Scientist-style tournament systems report expert novelty 3.64/5 on 11 of 15 goals, but the evaluation is small and subjective.
agent_test: Weak evidence; do not rely on it.

claim: Judge models favour their own family and low-perplexity text, through self-recognition (GPT-4 73.5% self-recognition; self-preference score 0.520 for GPT-4 in the largest of eight judges tested).
agent_test: Grade candidate novelty with a different-family judge or a mixed-family panel; compare scores for own-family vs other-family candidates.

claim: Pre-execution reviewer scores barely predict post-execution scores (AI ideas: excitement r about -0.32), while a fine-tuned predictor with retrieval predicts which of two ideas wins at 64.4% vs experts 48.9%; frontier models alone were near random.
agent_test: Log candidate novelty before and after a verification step and check whether the pre-step rating predicts the post-step one.

claim: Near-purpose, far-mechanism inspirations gave more good ideas (46% vs 37% random vs 30% near-domain; mixed-model probability 0.71 vs 0.28 and 0.27) in a human crowd design task: the Uzzi pattern in an experiment.
agent_test: Compare one far element added to a near frame against all-near and all-far sets at equal tokens, with blind ratings.

claim: Diverse multi-agent teams with a leader beat one self-reflecting agent on LLM-judged proposal quality (+0.46 overall, human blind A/B 87.5% of 40 pairs), but all-junior teams did not (7.73 vs 7.75) and gains flatten past 3 agents; not equal tokens.
agent_test: Run 3 mixed-persona samples with an integrating step vs one agent with the same token budget.

claim: Models are homogeneous across families (pairwise similarity 71% to 82%; 61.2% of pairs above 0.8 even at min-p temperature 2.0), so pooling models adds little; showing earlier answers in context (in-context regeneration) roughly reaches human-writer diversity.
agent_test: Generate candidates sequentially with earlier ones visible; measure distinct-k per token against parallel sampling.

claim: Path novelty in code and maths is costly: correct-and-novel rates fall as constraints are added; reasoning scaffolds (self-correction, planning) raise correctness but cut divergence, only MCTS raised divergence; MATH accuracy does not predict novelty (GPT-4o 76.6% MATH, novel/correct under 50%); capability only weakly predicts idea originality (r=0.357).
agent_test: On maths and planning tasks, test 'name the standard method, then forbid it' against plain retry at equal tokens.

claim: Uzzi's hit-rate result is robust inside WoS to field fixed effects (243 subfields), a top-1% hit cut and reference-count controls, and tail cuts at the 1st to 20th percentile; it vanishes at the 30th percentile and above; peak near the 85th percentile of conventionality. Null model: 10 degree-preserving rewired networks. No outside-WoS replication opened.
agent_test: None; descriptive.

claim: Text-embedding novelty has a small link to authors' self-rated newness (r=.170, p<.01, title-based Novel100; N=2,081 scientists, 321 biomedical); similar to the weak journal-pair link, so no cheap proxy is strong. Not compared against Uzzi-style scores.
agent_test: Treat any cheap proxy as a weak prior; validate against blind labels before use.

claim: A shared LLM strategy list made later unaided human ideas less original (Dunn p=0.009, N=460 in that experiment) and more similar to each other.
agent_test: Check whether a fixed scaffold narrows the agent's candidate set versus no scaffold.
